Run and Persist One GLOW Scan Unit

Source: R/run_scan_unit.R
run_scan_unit.Rd

Runs one scan unit: builds the unit's regions and filter(s) with build_scan_regions, runs glow_scan_chunk (once for gene/window; once per category for coding), and writes the per-unit flat results table plus the policy-gated sidecars, emitting log lines through logger. A scan "unit" is one chromosome (gene/coding) or one genome chunk (window). The thin per-type entry scripts resolve the prepared inputs and call this with region_type set.

run_scan_unit(
  gds_path,
  null_model,
  pi_models,
  pi_features,
  reference_medians,
  b_func = NULL,
  b_model = NULL,
  region_type,
  config,
  results_path,
  output_dir,
  output_policy,
  chr = NULL,
  chunk = NULL,
  unit_id = NULL,
  staar_context = NULL,
  use_spa = NULL,
  z_scale = 1,
  max_regions = NA_integer_,
  progress_every = 0L,
  logger = NULL,
  n_cores = NULL,
  verbose = 0
)

Arguments

gds_path

Character. Path to the unit's GDS/aGDS file.

null_model, pi_models, pi_features, reference_medians

The resolved prepared inputs (from prepare_scan_run), passed to the scan engine. reference_medians is this unit's chromosome's annotation-median cache.

b_func, b_model

The B source (exactly one non-NULL), passed to the engine.

region_type

Character: "gene", "window", "coding" or "noncoding" (the gene-centric non-coding masks, see the section below).

config

An environment or named list of resolved config values. Used for the region/filter build (see build_scan_regions) and the engine knobs ld_threshold, mac_threshold, collapse_method, output_format.

results_path

Character. Path the flat results table is written to.

output_dir

Character. Directory under which sidecar folders (evidence/, staar_detail/, result_objects/) are created.

output_policy

A glow_output_policy.

chr

Integer or character chromosome (required for gene/coding; for window it is taken from chunk). Default NULL.

chunk

A single-row genome-chunk data.frame (required for window). Default NULL.

unit_id

Character or integer used in the sidecar filenames and log lines to identify the unit (e.g. the chr number or chunk id). Default derived from chr / chunk$chunk_id.

staar_context

A STAAR context or NULL (STAAR off). Default NULL.

use_spa, z_scale

Threaded to the engine (see glow_scan_chunk). Defaults NULL / 1.

max_regions

Integer or NA. If not NA, cap the regions to the first max_regions (smoke-test; the --max-genes/--max-windows parallel). Default NA.

progress_every

Integer threaded to the engine. Default 0L.

logger

A function(msg) for log lines, or NULL (silent). Default NULL.

n_cores

Integer or NULL (default). Forked workers for this unit. NULL reads config$n_cores and falls back to 1. With more than one, the regions are grouped into blocks by size (see the section "Scheduling over the workers"), each block runs glow_scan_chunk in a forked worker with its own GDS handle (parallel::mclapply, dynamic dispatch), and the block outputs are merged and restored to the regions table's order by label, so the written table equals the single-core one. The progress callback is off inside the workers; the parent logs one scheduler line per regions table and one line per finished block. Forking is unavailable on Windows (a value above 1 warns and runs serially). Memory scales with the workers, since each holds its own genotype and LD matrices.

verbose

Integer threaded to the engine. Default 0.

Value

Invisibly, a named list with results (the written flat table), summary (a 1-row tally; the engine summary for gene/window, or a per-category-stacked summary for coding), errors (a data.frame), and results_path.

Details

Compute order (coding). Categories are looped outer — one glow_scan_chunk call per category over the gene table, with the category's filter as the only difference — so each call is exactly a gene-style call and coding reuses the scan engine unchanged. Each call's result table is tagged with a category column and the tables are row-bound; the combined table leads with label, chr, category (gene-first column order) and is sorted (start, category) so the on-disk ROW order is gene-first (each gene's categories together at its genomic position), matching the gene-first aggregation output.

Region summary. region_summary is enabled for region_type %in% c("gene") (gene and custom-gene-list scans both dispatch as "gene") and disabled for window/coding, so the gene flat table carries the 7 region-summary columns and the other schemas are unchanged.

Writes. The flat results table is written to results_path (CSV by default, or fst when config$output_format == "fst"). Policy-gated sidecars (evidence, staar_detail, result_objects) are written under output_dir into their own on-demand folders, only when both the policy flag is on and the scan engine produced the artifact (so no orphan/empty folders).

Gene-centric non-coding masks

For region_type = "noncoding" the unit is a chromosome and build_scan_regions returns one regions table per mask of config$noncoding_categories (default the eight masks of GLOWr::noncoding_masks()), built once from the chromosome's annotations by GLOWr::define_regions_noncoding. Each mask's table is run like a coding category (the label check, max_regions and the scheduler apply per table; region_summary is off), the rows are tagged with category, and the combined table leads with label, chr, category and is sorted gene-first by the gene anchor of noncoding_gene_anchor (a gene's masks together, because their candidate spans differ), then by mask. A row's start, end and midpoint describe the candidate span, which is wide for an enhancer far from its gene. Two sidecars are written beside the flat table on every completed unit, for the aggregation's completeness table: the error table as <results_path stem>_errors.csv (zero rows when no cell errored, so a rerun never leaves an earlier run's errors beside a clean table) and the per-mask tallies (cells attempted, tested, skipped for an empty set or a single rare variant, errored) as <results_path stem>_summary.csv. The log carries one line per mask with the genes, the selected records and the links.

Large genes

For region_type = "gene" the unit's variant index is passed to build_scan_regions, which tiles every gene with more GDS records than config$gene_max_records into segments of config$gene_segment_bp (see that function). The log states how many genes were segmented and into how many segments.

Scheduling over the workers

With n_cores > 1 the regions of a table are not run in genomic order. Heavy genes sit next to each other on the genome, and a block of consecutive regions that holds several of them keeps one worker busy long after the others have finished. Instead, every region's GDS record count \(n_i\) is read from the unit's variant index (two binary searches per region, no genotype read; the gene segmentation's n_records is reused where present) and its cost is taken as \(c_i = n_i^2\), a heuristic that lets a few heavy regions dominate the sums. With \(C = \sum_i c_i\) and \(\tau = C / (8\,\mathrm{n\_cores})\), a region with \(c_i \ge \tau\) forms a block of its own; the remaining regions, in decreasing cost, are packed into blocks that close at 25 regions or when the next region would push the summed cost above \(\tau\); and the blocks are dispatched in decreasing summed cost, so the heaviest work starts first and the light blocks fill the tail. When \(C = 0\) the regions keep their order in blocks of 25. Each region is computed independently of its block, so the merged rows are the serial ones; the merge puts the flat rows, the error rows and the sidecar entries back in the order of the labels in the regions table. This needs unique labels, which the function enforces at every n_cores: a repeated label stops the run with the duplicates named, because the sidecars and the error table are keyed by label and a duplicate already loses information silently in the serial path. For the coding type each category's pass over the gene table is scheduled this way, one category after another. The log's scheduler line gives the number of blocks, how many are a heavy region alone, the heaviest region and \(\tau\); each block line gives the block's region count, its heaviest record count, its tally and its wall time, so the reader sees where the unit's time went.

See also

build_scan_regions, glow_scan_chunk, glow_output_policy, prepare_scan_run

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
bundle <- prepare_scan_run(env, "runs/myrun/outputs", chroms = 22L)
run_scan_unit(
  gds_path = "data/chr22.gds",
  null_model = bundle$null_model, pi_models = bundle$pi_models,
  pi_features = bundle$pi_features, reference_medians = meds22,
  b_func = bundle$b_func, b_model = bundle$b_model,
  region_type = "gene", chr = 22, config = env,
  results_path = "runs/myrun/outputs/results/glow_chr22.csv",
  output_dir = "runs/myrun/outputs",
  output_policy = glow_output_policy(), logger = message)
} # }
